summary: OpenAI describes a temporary slowdown of frontier RL training and new security, monitoring and alignment measures after preliminary evidence that its upcoming Astra model may cross the Critical cybersecurity capability threshold under its Preparedness Framework.

mechanisms.reason: OpenAI explicitly paused RL training and continues to hold its largest planned frontier RL run to allow safeguards to catch up, temporarily reducing training activity.
mechanisms.quote: Our largest planned frontier RL run remains on hold while we conduct smaller-scale training and evaluations to assess model behavior, validate our safeguards, and establish more evidence of alignment before proceeding.

mechanisms.reason: The new monitoring system adds a stated ~20% compute overhead to monitored inference, increasing the work required per token rather than reducing it.
mechanisms.quote: Our current estimates put monitoring overhead at roughly 20% of the inference compute being monitored, though the cost varies substantially across training and evaluation workloads.

mechanisms.reason: The document reports preliminary evidence that an upcoming model may cross a named critical cybersecurity capability threshold, indicating a step change in capability, though not yet confirmed or released.
mechanisms.quote: preliminary evidence that one of our upcoming models, Astra, may meet the Critical cybersecurity capability threshold under our Preparedness Framework

practices.reason: The multistage activation-classifier and escalation monitoring pipeline is a concrete safety monitoring architecture an engineering team could study for its own model-behavior monitoring, though it is described as internal infrastructure rather than a transferable tool.
practices.quote: This new monitoring setup is multistage, starting with activation classifiers (detectors that inspect a model’s internal activity) that run at every sampled token and escalate potential concerns to increasingly sophisticated and high-compute automated investigators.

practices.reason: Alignment training changes such as improved reward models and honesty training are described directionally but without enough method detail to replicate.
practices.quote: This includes improving reward models to better detect and discourage unsafe behavior across tasks and environments; training models to be more honest about their actions, capabilities, and limitations; and reducing behaviors that exploit weaknesses in rewards, graders, tools, or oversight.

notable_reason: A frontier lab disclosing that it paused its largest planned RL training run over preliminary evidence of a critical cyber capability threshold is a rare, concrete safety-pacing decision worth tracking.
